info.title: Salus Open API
info.description:
Salus Open API for gateways, devices, history, energy, alerts, and EV chargers.

Call POST /login, copy access_token from the response, then paste it into Authorize to try the other endpoints.

Premium Lite routes live under `/premium-lite/`. EV Charger routes live under `/ev-charger/`.

get.description:
Occupant profile for the logged-in user (same source as the Premium app).

Public fields only: name, email, country, language, phone, and display
preferences. Account identifiers, consent, privacy, and gateway access
are not included. Gateway access is GET /premium-lite/gateways.

get.description:
Occupant profile for the logged-in user.

Public fields only: name, email, country, language, and phone.
Display preferences (hour, date, temperature) are not returned.
Account identifiers, consent, and privacy fields are not included.

`country` is the English country name shown in the EV app
(for example `Romania`).

get.description:
Gateways the occupant can access, with permission level per gateway.

Access levels: O owner, F family, G guest, I installer. When is_temp_access is true,
start_time and end_time are UTC datetimes; otherwise null. created_at and updated_at are UTC.
Device codes of children on this gateway.

200.description: Child device codes for this gateway

schema.description: Array of device_code strings. Empty array when none.

schema.title: Device details
schema.description: Snapshot for this device: always includes identifiers and online flag; other keys depend on product type.

model.description: Device model identifier from the device record (same as the model segment in device_code).

connected.description: True when the device is online and reachable on the network; false when offline or status is unknown. Same signal as GET /premium-lite/status/{device_code}.

last_message_rssi.description: RF signal strength of last message (RSSI), vendor raw integer (typically dBm-related). No unit conversion applied.

temperature_display_step_granularity.description: DialRF/Quantum local temperature display step: 0.1°, or 0.5°C / 1°F depending on temperature display mode.

cooling_setpoint.description: Cooling target in °C. Vendor payload is °C ×100; API divides by 100. Comfort range is typically about 5–35 °C.

heating_setpoint.description: Heating target in °C. Vendor payload is °C ×100; API divides by 100. Comfort range is typically about 5–35 °C.

hold_mode.description: Thermostat hold mode. DialRF overlay writes follow_schedule (0) or permanent_hold (2); device may also report temporary_hold (1), holiday (6), frost_or_off (7). Writes use SetHoldType.

current_temperature.description: Room temperature in °C. Vendor payload is °C ×100; API divides by 100. Display rounding (°F / CoolingControl step) and invalid sentinels (8000, ±32768) are not applied here.

setpoint_changing_enabled.description: Whether the dial/UI may change the setpoint. Vendor LockKey 0 → true (unlocked), 1 → false (locked). DialRF settings label this as Change setpoint Yes/No (Yes=0). Window-protection 98/99 left unmapped (pass through).

max_cool_setpoint.description: Maximum cooling setpoint in °C. Vendor payload is °C ×100; API divides by 100. Typical comfort range about 5–35 °C. UI may also show °F; that conversion is not applied here.

max_heat_setpoint.description: Maximum heating setpoint in °C. Vendor payload is °C ×100; API divides by 100. Typical comfort range about 5–35 °C. UI may also show °F; that conversion is not applied here.

min_cool_setpoint.description: Minimum cooling setpoint in °C. Vendor payload is °C ×100; API divides by 100. Typical comfort range about 5–35 °C. UI may also show °F; that conversion is not applied here.

min_heat_setpoint.description: Minimum heating setpoint in °C. Vendor payload is °C ×100; API divides by 100. Typical comfort range about 5–35 °C. UI may also show °F; that conversion is not applied here.

outdoor_sensor_probe.description: Installer Sensor Probe mode (Salus Settings). 0 No Sensor Connected; 1 Sensor Probe Connected (external temp, often floor); 2 DEW Point Sensor Connected where offered; 3 Occupancy Sensor; 4 S1/S2 Input. API enum tokens below; ScheduleType refines occupancy/S1-S2 state when probe is 3 or 4.

paired_to.description: What this thermostat is paired to. DialRF setup is wiring-centre only: 1–9 → wiring_center_zone_N; -3 → not_paired. Unmapped vendor codes pass through as raw integers.

running_state.description: Active HVAC demand decoded from vendor RunningState (bit0 heating, bit1 cooling).

humidity.description: Relative humidity in percent. On DialRF/Quantum, Premium reads SunnySetpoint_x100 via getHumidity() and shows the raw integer as % (e.g. 38 → 38%). Do not divide by 100 — the _x100 suffix is legacy naming here, not a ×100 scale.

system_mode.description: HVAC system mode (heat/cool/off). Same codes as vendor SystemMode: 0 off, 1 auto, 3 cool, 4 heat, 5 emergency_heating. DialRF/Quantum overlays write heat/cool via SetSystemMode; off/auto may still be reported. On Premium, live controls often read SystemMode (non-_a); Open API for DialRF exposes this _a twin. UI also uses mode to pick which setpoint slider is active — OAPI keeps setpoints separate.

temperature_display_mode.description: Device temperature unit. Vendor TemperatureDisplayMode: 0 → celsius, 1 → fahrenheit (TemperatureDisplayModeType / SettingOptions). Same on sIT600TH, sTherUIS, sIRTH.

time_format.description: Clock display format on the thermostat. 0 → 12_hour, 1 → 24_hour (Premium Settings dropdown). Writes use SetTimeFormat24Hour.

valve_protection.description: Valve exercise/protection enabled. Vendor ValveProtection: 0 → false (off/disabled), 1 → true (on/enabled). Same on sIT600TH / sIT600HW / sComm dropdowns.

name.description: Display name you choose for the device (short label). Vendor may send a plain string or a JSON blob with `deviceName` (Premium getDeviceName / buildPublishNamePayload).

firmware_version.description: Premium EU DialRF / Quantum / RF info screen: parse whole FirmwareVersion as hex, ÷10, one decimal (convertFirmwareVersionForEU). Quantum Plus (SQ610RF*) is not on that path (category check skips it → raw). US DialRF often stays raw. Other families use different recipes.

EvChargerListItem.description:
One charger on this account. `model` is the charger model name shown
in the app. `charger_name` is the name set on the charger.

device_code.description: Identifier for this charger. Use it as `{device_code}` on other EV charger routes.

model.description: Charger model name, as shown in About Device (for example EV7EU).

serial_number.description: Serial number printed on the charger label. `-` when unset.

ownership.description: Whether you own this charger (`own`) or it was shared with you (`shared`).

charger_name.description: Display name set on the charger; null when unset or unavailable.

EvChargerDevice.description:
Charger properties. `device_code`, `model`, `serial_number`, and
`charger_name` are always present (`serial_number` is `-` when unset;
`charger_name` is null when unset). Other fields appear only for the
models, settings, and states that use them, and are omitted otherwise.
The response does not add keys outside this set.

model.description: Charger model name, as shown in About Device (for example EV7EU).

connection_status.description: Whether the charger is currently online and can be reached.

charger_name.description: Display name set on the charger; null when unset or unavailable.

serial_number.description: Serial number printed on the charger label. `-` when unset.

company.description: The company that manufactured the charger.

firmware_version.description: The firmware version currently installed on the charger.

update_available.description:
True when a newer firmware version is available for this charger.
False when the charger is already up to date.

update_status.description:
Progress of a firmware update (Installed, Downloading, Download Failed,
Installing, Installation Failed, or Idle). In-progress statuses older
than 15 minutes, when the charger is already on the latest firmware,
are shown as Idle.

charger_status.description:
What the charger is doing right now. Some statuses only include
`status`; a live session also includes power, energy, updated_on
and duration. When `status` is `suspended_evse`, `pause_reason`
explains why charging is paused. When paused for `schedule`,
`charging_starts_at` is the off-peak window start (HH:mm).

status.description: Charging state in lower case (for example charging, available).

pause_reason.description:
Why charging is paused while `status` is `suspended_evse`.
Possible values: `schedule` (waiting for the off-peak window),
`load_curtailment` (the home is using too much power), or
`randomised_delay` (a short random delay before starting).
Omitted when charging is not paused or the reason is unavailable.

charging_starts_at.description:
Time of day (HH:mm) when charging is expected to begin again.
Included only when charging is paused for `schedule`; omitted
for other pause reasons or when not paused.

energy_supplied.description: Energy delivered this session (for example "2109.21 kWh").

updated_on.description: When the meter energy reading was last updated.

duration.description: How long the current or just-finished session has been running.

is_charger_locked.description: Whether the charger is locked so it cannot be used (`Locked` or `Unlocked`).

is_connector_locked.description: Whether the charging connector/cable is locked (`Locked` or `Unlocked`).

plug_and_charge.description: Whether charging starts automatically when you plug in (On or Off).

randomised_delay.description: Whether the charger waits a short random time before it starts (On or Off).

boost_duration.description: How long a boost charge runs when you temporarily override the off-peak schedule.

off_peak_schedule.description: Daily off-peak window. When enabled is off, schedule is an empty object.

enabled.description: Whether the off-peak window is active (`on` or `off`).

static_load_management.description: The charging current limit set for this charger (for example "16A").

max_charge_current.description: The highest charging current this charger supports (for example "32A").

load_curtailment.description: Household electricity supply limit used for load curtailment (for example "20A" or "OFF").

curtailment_threshold.description: Displayed amp limit derived from household capacity (for example "16A" or "OFF").

load_curtailment_active.description:
True when load curtailment is currently limiting charging. False
when load curtailment is off or not actively limiting power. Shown
on single-phase chargers. Omitted when not reported.

home_current.description: Derived household current excluding the charger (for example "9.0 A"). Single-phase only.

available_current.description: Derived remaining current the charger can draw (for example "7.0 A"). Single-phase only.

clamp_status.description:
Whether the charger can measure how much power the home is using
(`Valid` or `Invalid`). `Invalid` means the reading is unreliable,
so charging may not be limited correctly. Shown on single-phase
chargers. Omitted when not reported.

nfc_cards.description: NFC cards allowed to start a charge.

duration.description: Session length as hours and minutes.

tag_id.description: NFC / RFID card used for the session, when present.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null when complete.

error_code.description:
Fault code as shown in the Error Log (for example `0x00010000`).
Combined codes are split into the matching known faults when more
than one applies.

title.description: Short label for the fault. Localized via `language`. Null when unknown.

description.description: Longer fault text. Localized via `language`. Null when unknown.
description.example: Charger front cover is not correctly installed. Install it properly and charger will resume normal operation.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null when complete.
